description:
fz's `defstruct` accepts only a bracketed list of bare atoms. Elixir's
keyword-with-defaults forms are rejected at the PARSER, and even if they parsed,
`StructDef` has nowhere to put a default.

DECIDE FIRST whether fz `defstruct` supports default values. This is a language
feature question, not a bug on a critical path.

## Repro

    defmodule Point do
      defstruct x: 1, y: 2
    end
    fn main() do
      p = %Point{}
      dbg(p.x)
    end

    error[parse/expected-token]: expected `[`, got KwKey("x")
      --> defstruct_defaults.fz:2:13

Bracketed keyword form fails differently:

    defstruct [x: 1, y: 2]
    error[parse/expected-token]: expected `]`, got Int(1)
      --> defstruct_defaults2.fz:2:17

## Where it actually fails

`parse_struct_item`, src/compiler2/frontdoor.rs:325-351. It requires `[`
(`self.expect(&Tok::LBrack, "`[`")?`), then loops accepting
`Tok::Atom(name) | Tok::Ident(name) | Tok::KwKey(name)` as a field name and looks
for `,` or `]`. A `KwKey` is consumed as the field name and its default
expression is DISCARDED at the token level, so the following `Int(1)` is
unexpected.

The keyword-list surface itself is fine -- `dbg([x: 1, y: 2])` prints
`[{:x, 1}, {:y, 2}]`. Only `defstruct`'s hand-rolled field loop refuses it.

## What the old ticket got wrong

It blamed `parse_struct_form` (quoted_surface.rs:647-655) calling
`fields.list_atom_names()`, on the theory that keyword pairs arrive as 2-tuples
and `atom_name()` errors. THAT CODE IS NEVER REACHED -- frontdoor rejects the
form and drops the default before any quoted surface exists. Start in
frontdoor.rs, not quoted_surface.rs.

## What is still true

- `parse_struct_form` does call `fields.list_atom_names()?`
  (quoted_surface.rs:653) and would need widening once frontdoor emits pairs.
- `StructDef` is `fields: Vec<String>` + span (structdef.rs:41-44) -- no
  defaults. Adding them is a store-shape change touching every landed consumer:
  resolve StructRecord, protocol-impl-target, body.rs `MakeStruct` lowering, and
  backend `struct_schemas`.

## Elixir's answer

    defmodule Point do defstruct x: 1, y: 2 end
    %Point{}                       => %Point{x: 1, y: 2}
    q = %Point{y: 9}; {q.x, q.y}   => {1, 9}
    defmodule P2 do defstruct [:a, b: 5] end
    %P2{}                          => %P2{a: nil, b: 5}

So: bare-keyword form, mixed `[:a, b: 5]` form, bare atoms default to nil, and a
`%A{}` literal omitting a field gets that field's default.

## Checks

- `defstruct x: 1, y: 2` and `defstruct [x: 1, y: 2]` both parse.
- `defstruct [:a, b: 5]` parses; `%P2{}` yields a = nil and b = 5.
- `%Point{}` yields {1, 2}; `%Point{y: 9}` yields {1, 9}.
- Existing bare-atom fixtures still pass unchanged
  (fixtures2/00081_struct_type_alias_fields.fz uses
  `defstruct [:first, :last, :step]`).
- A defaults-bearing fixture matches an `.oracle.exs` on interp, run and build.
title: defstruct rejects Elixir's keyword-with-defaults form; frontdoor drops the default and StructDef carries no defaults
